title: Meeting clarinettist Raymond Burke
summary: Burke told him he is out of practice; Polites finds his clarinet tone beautiful and is amused to advise him.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Who were the great clarinetists? Favorites and rivals

blocks.x: How did you like meeting Raymond Burke? Describe that for Paul.

Raymond Burke is, I hadn't heard him at all. I just heard that he's supposed to be the best white clarinet player in New Orleans. I met him yesterday and he said, I don't play much in front of public. I'm a bit afraid to. They all play too fast. I'm out of practice. I don't know what it is. If you think it's because I don't play very much these days that I find it hard to keep up with it. Well I answered what seemed to be logical. Naturally I suppose if you're out of practice you're going to find it hard to just pick up a clarinet and play. You have to warm up. You have to sort of practice a bit each day if possible. It seems so ridiculous that I should be telling Ray Burke all about it. It's amazing that a chap, I've heard a bit of his stuff since. He plays a beautiful clarinet. I like it very much. He plays with a really beautiful tone. He's a subtle sort of player. It seems amazing that a chap who can play such beautiful music should even be asking questions like this. Particularly of me. It's quite a joke.
